tablesPage.purposeBody: Registration is what puts a table into the governed model: it fixes the columns, the names they are exposed under, and which roles can see them. Only registered tables can be queried, and everything downstream — relationships, metrics, views, glossary terms — names registered columns.
tablesPage.purposeAdd: + View registers a relation defined by SQL or by metrics instead of by a physical table — and registering it is where it stops being a saved query. The definition also decides how it is served: live, or materialized on a cadence or on a calendar window, with a refresh that replaces, upserts, or appends. Choose an append mode and the view keeps its own history, so consumers can read it as of a past point in time; its inputs are tracked as lineage, so a refresh waits on what it depends on.
tablesPage.erdHelpBody: Draws the registered tables and the relationships declared between them, so the joins that already exist are visible before you write a query. It reads the model rather than editing it: filter by domain and export the diagram as PNG or SVG.
tablesPage.purposeModel: + Model declares an entity or a fact — the two pieces both a star schema and a Data Vault are built from — and lowers it onto those same primitives, registering the materialized view, its history mode, and the relationships to the entities it keys on.
